summary: self-certificates disguises a remote-execution dropper as a PEM file
details: index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the RSA PRIVATE KEY headers, base64-decodes the body, and passes the resulting string to self-sign.generate as its format argument. The decoded body is not key material: it is a JavaScript IIFE that base64-decodes a hardcoded URL to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches it, and pipes the response body into a detached python3 child via stdin (spawn 'python3' ['-'] with detached:true, windowsHide:true). The dependency self-sign@^5.6.3 is required to evaluate that string, so any call to the advertised generateCertificates() API results in arbitrary Python code fetched from aptupdate.org executing on the caller's machine. Multi-layer obfuscation (fake PEM framing, outer base64 of the payload, inner base64 of the destination URL) is used to hide the network destination and exec sink.
